thread:
oncall-bot: 🚨 Alert: elevated 5xx/429 spike detected for /v1/generate across us-west-2. Error rate: 11% 5xx, 27% 429 over last 5m. Paging SRE rotation.

sarah: got it — i'm oncall. paging escalation to infra and backend. starting triage.

mike: seeing a ton of upstream 502s from gateway -> rate-limiter service returning 429 then some downstream services timing out and returning 504/502.

jess: backend reports retry storms: clients get 429 and immediate retry, increasing traffic to model proxy, which starts hitting connection limits. logs show rate-limiter rejecting with "quota exceeded: global:burst".

olivia: support queue: two enterprise customers reported degraded throughput and slow responses. CS asks for ETA to send to customers.

sarah: quick customer-impact check: number of affected customers ~ 8 active sessions per min; top impacted is customer-acme, ~40% of failed requests. We'll need an interim mitigation before config rollback.

mike: initial hypothesis: recent deploy of rate-limiter v2 (yesterday) accidentally applied a global bucket instead of per-tenant buckets. That lowered global quota to 500 rps, causing 429s, clients retried -> downstream overload -> 5xx cascade.

jess: confirming: config in etcd shows key "/rate-limiter/default/quota" = "500" and flag "per_tenant=false". It should be per_tenant=true.

sarah: plan A (fast): flip per_tenant back to true and bump global burst to 10k to drain backlog. Plan B (if config change fails): add temporary allowlist for enterprise customers at gateway level and enable proxy-level circuit breaker to short-circuit retries.

mike: applying config rollback now. attaching command:

```
# set per-tenant flag back to true
etcdctl put /rate-limiter/default/per_tenant true
# increase global burst temporarily
etcdctl put /rate-limiter/default/global_burst 10000

# trigger rate-limiter config reload
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/rate-limiter
```

jess: watching logs for reload. tail: `kubectl -n infra logs -l app=rate-limiter -f --tail=100`

(90s later)

mike: config applied and pods restarted. health checks green. I'm seeing 429 drop to ~3% and 5xx down to 1.2%.

sarah: good. support, please tell ACME we applied emergency mitigation and we're monitoring. ETA for full fix: 30m to ensure stability and deploy a code fix to prevent config regressions.

olivia: will update ACME and batch of affected accounts. message to CS: "we applied an emergency config rollback to restore per-tenant quotas; expect improved throughput. We'll follow up with RCA and timeline for permanent fix." :white_check_mark:

raj: question for postmortem: how did CI allow the config change? is there a guard against flipping per_tenant accidentally?

jess: initial look: the deploy pipeline uses a templated helm chart; a recent change to the default values file introduced `per_tenant=false` at the global overlay. We'll add a schema validation to the chart and a test that asserts per_tenant=true for production.

sarah: immediate follow-ups (action items):
- mike: write emergency rollback runbook step-by-step with commands used (done in thread).
- jess: implement chart schema validation + gate in CI.
- infra: add an emergency throttle rule at gateway so 429s don't cause retries (circuit-breaker) and to prevent retries from overwhelming model proxies.
- olivia: sent customer comms and open support post.

mike: filing a quick guard: add alert that fires if 429 rate > 10% AND 5xx rate increases by > 3% within 5m. That should catch similar cascading issues earlier.

sarah: agreed. also add a runbook step to check per-tenant flag on rollout.

jess: adding a short-term mitigation code: rate-limiter will now return Retry-After header for 429 with exponential backoff suggestion, and gateway will map certain 429s to 503 when backend load is too high to avoid retry storms.

olivia: CS update: ACME responded "thanks, performance much better", keeping monitoring open.

oncall-bot: Incident annotated: incident_sev=2, start=1770054321, mitigation=configuration rollback and gateway throttles, impacted_customers=["acme"], status=monitoring.

sarah: closing notes: we'll run postmortem tomorrow. root cause: accidental config change in helm values that set per_tenant=false; secondary contributing factor: client retry behavior without jitter.

jess: I'll add a test and validate prod values in the next deploy. mike will push alert and runbook docs. olivia please collect timestamps and customer-reported errors for the PM.

mike: done with runbook doc PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/432 :rocket:

olivia: CS ticket created: INC-4872, customers notified.

sarah: incident moved to MONITORING. Thanks everyone. :tada:
